stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

I’m happy to help you build a function that pulls game data for 2019, but I’ll need a bit more detail first:

1. **What kind of “games” are you interested in?**  
   - *Sports matches* (e.g., football/soccer fixtures, NBA games, etc.)  
   - *Video games* released in 2019 (titles, platforms, release dates, etc.)  
   - *Other types* (board games, esports tournaments, etc.)

2. **Do you already have an API or data source in mind?**  
   - For sports, common APIs include [football-data.org](https://www.football-data.org/), [sportsdata.io](https://sportsdata.io/), or [ESPN’s API](https://espn.com/apis).  
   - For video games, popular options are the [RAWG Video Games Database](https://rawg.io/apidocs) or the [IGDB API](https://api-docs.igdb.com/).  
   - If you’re looking at board games, the [BoardGameGeek API](https://boardgamegeek.com/wiki/page/BGG_XML_API) might be relevant.

3. **Do you have any authentication requirements?**  
   - Many of these services require an API key or OAuth token. If you already have one, let me know the format (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer <token>`).

Once I know which domain and API you’d like to target, I can draft a concrete function using the `requests_get` tool that fetches the 2019 data for you.
